title: Forensic: how was +01:00 applied to Korea/Taiwan imports, and is the pathway closed?
description: 526 Import files (Netherlands 269, Taiwan 120, South Korea 137) carry a jetlag-written XMP-exif DateTimeOriginal stamped +01:00. NL +01:00 was plausibly intentional (camera country-zone, UK-era). But Daniel is certain he only ever declared +09:00 for Korea (and +08:00 for Taiwan) — never +01:00 — so a run applied a zone he did not specify. Suspects: app persisting the last-used timezone across sessions/profiles (AppState), a profile-level default, or a batch run over all of Import with a stale zone. Oddity that may narrow it: Taiwan wrong-zone and untouched files interleave BY DAY (2025-07-17 has 9 wrong-zone + 8 untouched), so it was not a single clean sweep of everything present. Task: reconstruct the pathway from app/pipeline code and git history, and verify post-#140 behavior (gate + requires_force_timezone) plus the one-timezone-rule work (jetlag-z1e) actually close it — note the sweep victims were zone-less at the time, so the #140 gate alone does NOT block a stale declared zone being applied to naive files. Evidence tables in session scratchpad census (2026-08-12).

title: Clock writes must reach the track atoms
description: write_quicktime_createdate() sends -QuickTime:CreateDate= and -QuickTime:MediaCreateDate=. Real-file evidence (Import/ Taiwan sample, 2026-08-12): the MediaCreateDate write DOES reach all per-track mdhd atoms; the atom never written is TrackCreateDate (tkhd) — that is where the pre-correction original survives. Spec: corrections write every clock field so any application reads the corrected time. ORDERING CONSTRAINT: the provenance tag (one free-form write-once metadata tag recording the file's initial dates/filename before jetlag's first write; never read back as a source, never used by the app, invisible to the user — exists purely for out-of-app recovery) must land with or before this change, because today the untouched tkhd atoms are the accidental backup and this change would overwrite them. Handoff items 3+4; timestamp-source-of-truth.md §Writes/§Provenance.

title: Pipeline timezone-mismatch block becomes informational; app assent wiring
description: media-pipeline.py ~707 still exits 1 on provided-vs-embedded mismatch even in dry-run (introduced by #111 against time-correction-pipeline-step.md:99). Agreed flow (PR #140 implements the per-file half in fix-media-timestamp.py): dry-run always previews with conflicts as data (requires_force_timezone per file), apply without --force-timezone refused. Pipeline: emit timezone_conflict as informational in dry-run and continue; app: diff table highlights conflicted rows from requires_force_timezone, apply button prompts assent which re-runs with --force-timezone. UI holds no logic beyond assembling the command. Depends on PR #140 merging.

title: Bundle gyroflow as optional Settings-driven install
description: Bare-binary bundling from #121 never worked (signature invalid outside app bundle, missing mdk/Qt frameworks); dead binary removed in #139. Approved design: resolve order /Applications/Gyroflow.app -> ~/Library/Application Support/Jetlag/tools/Gyroflow.app -> which gyroflow -> configured path; download-gyroflow.sh installs the FULL app into Application Support (never inside the signed Jetlag bundle) and reports existing installs instead of downloading; presence exposed script-side as data (@@present/@@path/@@source); app gates all gyroflow UI on that single flag; Settings row 'Stabilization (Gyroflow)' with Install button + progress. See docs/timestamp-fields.md-adjacent discussion in PR #139/#140.

title: Speed up the test suite: module-call tests, xdist, bundle-phase outputs
description: Full scripts suite takes minutes because tests are integration-shaped: nearly every test spawns python -> script CLI -> exiftool/ffprobe per case, on real files. The subprocess-to-module-calls migration (docs/specs/completed/subprocess-to-module-calls.md) covered media-pipeline's internal calls but the TEST SUITE was never migrated and still pays full process-spawn tax per test. Work: (1) quick wins — run pytest with -n auto (pytest-xdist; tests are tmpdir-isolated), and declare outputs on the Xcode 'Bundle scripts' build phase so incremental builds skip the per-build pip install (Xcode already warns about it); (2) real fix — migrate tests that target logic to direct module calls (import via importlib like the pipeline does, assert on returned dataclasses and real file state, not @@ stdout), keeping a small deliberate set of true CLI-contract tests per script (arg parsing, @@ emission, exit codes). Rules: docs/testing.md still applies — file-state assertions stay; this changes HOW code is invoked, not what is asserted. STRICT SCOPE: test suite and build config only; never run anything against user media volumes.

title: App cannot tell a missing interpreter from a Command Line Tools stub
description: On a Mac without Xcode or CLT, /usr/bin/python3 triggers the developer-tools install dialog instead of running, so a user hits an opaque failure. See the open risk in docs/specs/python-runtime.md; the app should detect this and say what to install. (Migrated from TODO.md, added 2026-08-11.)

title: App bundle ships pytest and pyrefly (~35MB dev tooling)
description: requirements.txt mixes runtime deps (PyYAML, humanize) with dev-only tooling, and the Bundle scripts phase vendors all of it into Contents/Resources/scripts/site-packages — ~35MB of test tooling a user never runs. Split into requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt, vendor only the former. (Migrated from TODO.md, added 2026-08-11.)

title: Real idempotence test: reprocessing equals processing a pristine copy
description: test_fix_media_timestamp.py:60 is the only idempotence test; its fixture already carries a zoned DateTimeOriginal and runs with no declared timezone, exercising only the pass-through path that cannot regress. The assertion that catches real regressions: for each source in the ranking, reprocessing a corrected file yields what processing a pristine copy yields (relabelling corrections only; --time-offset excluded by design). Fixtures need a real QuickTime date written explicitly (ffmpeg template carries 0000:00:00) — see TestQuickTimeInstantVersusFilename for the pattern. From handoff test-debt + spec §Idempotence.

title: One rule for when --timezone is required, mirrored by app and script
description: Three sources disagree: the app demands --timezone whenever the fix-timestamps step is enabled (AppState.validateTimezone), the script requires it only for --infer-from-filename and --time-offset, and the CLI help claims it's only needed when DateTimeOriginal lacks a zone. Spec (timestamp-source-of-truth.md §--timezone): always required for the step — instants (ranks 1-2) need it as display zone, naive sources (5-8) need it to build one. Mirror one rule; UI holds no logic beyond assembling the command. Handoff item 6.

title: Read OffsetTimeOriginal to complete a bare DateTimeOriginal
description: OffsetTimeOriginal (EXIF 2.31) is always and only the ±HH:MM zone of DateTimeOriginal's digits — binary EXIF DTO is 19 chars with no room for an inline zone. Generic supplement rule: a DTO lacking an inline zone is completed by OffsetTimeOriginal when present (any container; occurs on stills in practice — photo profiles exist in media-profiles.yaml). Upgrades a bare DTO to a zoned source in the ranking. Also verify what exiftool does when writing a zoned DTO value to a still (auto-split into OffsetTimeOriginal, or dropped?). See docs/timestamp-fields.md.

title: Surface inferred camera zone in dry-run diff data
description: filename − QuickTime date, when a legal zone offset, IS the camera's zone setting at shoot time; computed in _quicktime_is_instant() and discarded. Emit as @@camera_zone_offset whenever a filename and usable QuickTime date coexist (regardless of which source wins) so the diff table can show camera zone vs embedded label vs declared zone — answers 'was the camera still on Taipei time?' from the dry run itself.

title: tag-media.py makes a separate exiftool read for Make/Model
description: get_existing_exif_camera() runs its own exiftool subprocess independent of any other data read for the file. For files where both EXIF and Finder tags need checking, this means 2 reads (tag list + exif) before deciding on writes. Low priority since these are already small reads, but could be merged if tag-media is ever extended to read more EXIF fields. (Migrated from TODO.md, added 2026-02-20.)

title: Rank bare Keys:CreationDate as a naive source instead of ignoring it
description: A Keys:CreationDate with no zone suffix and no Z is currently invisible to get_best_timestamp() — only the zoned (rank 4) and Z (rank 1) shapes match. Decision (docs/timestamp-fields.md ranking): bare shape ranks with bare DateTimeOriginal (rank 6), digits assumed local in the declared --timezone. No device known to write it bare; recorded as a decision rather than an accident.
